items.title: Call for help first and then rescue
items.core: Professional rescue always takes priority.
body: Describe the location, number of people and injuries.

items.title: Key points of cardiopulmonary resuscitation
items.core: Compression should be fast and deep, and continue until help arrives.
body: Compress at the standard frequency and cooperate with artificial respiration.

items.title: Compression first to stop bleeding
items.core: Most external bleeding can be controlled with direct compression.
body: Use a clean cloth to press continuously.
For severe limb bleeding, a tourniquet may be considered and the time recorded.

items.title: Cool the temperature first for burns and scalds
items.core: Immediate cooling can reduce the damage.
body: Rinse with running cold water for sufficient time.
Do not apply home remedies or prick blisters.

items.title: If a foreign object is stuck in the throat, first determine
items.core: whether you can cough and speak to decide what to do.
body: In case of complete obstruction, seek help immediately and perform rescue operations according to regulations.

items.title: 先确认现场安全
items.core: 施救者安全是前提。
body: Observe fire, electricity, cars and chemicals.
When in doubt, call for help first and don’t get too close.

items.title: 呼救说清位置和人数
items.core: 信息完整才能快速派出救援。
body: Report the number and status of the injured.

items.title: 多人现场要分工
items.core: 混乱会浪费黄金时间。
body: Designate one person to make the call.

items.title: 不要随意搬动伤者
items.core: 脊柱损伤可能因移动加重。
body: Unless the environment is dangerous, wait where you are.
Keep your head and neck stable.

items.title: 休克时平卧保暖
items.core: 循环不足需要减少消耗。
body: 让伤者平躺并抬高下肢。

items.title: 记录关键时间
items.core: 时间线对后续救治有用。

items.title: Do not leave while waiting
items.core: Injury conditions may change suddenly.

items.title: 服从现场调度
items.core: 专业指挥能减少重复劳动。

items.title: 做好基础防护
items.core: 避免交叉感染。
body: 使用一次性手套或隔离物。

items.title: Evacuate the crowd of onlookers
items.core: Onlookers will hinder rescue.
body: Please ask irrelevant personnel to leave.

items.title: Protect the privacy of the injured
items.core: It is not suitable to shoot and disseminate the scene.

items.title: Explain the process when handing over
items.core: Complete handover of information is more conducive to treatment.
body: Describe what happened and what was done.
Hand over the records and time points.

items.title: Make psychological adjustments afterwards
items.core: Witnessing an accident will have an impact.
body: Seek help if you continue to feel unwell.

items.title: Ensure your own safety before drowning rescue
items.core: Don’t blindly go into the water if you don’t know how to swim.
body: Toss a float or call first.
Check your breathing and keep warm when you get ashore.

items.title: Turn off the power first if you get an electric shock
items.core: It is dangerous to approach when it is electrified.
body: Cut off the power supply or separate it with insulation.
Check your breathing and seek medical attention as soon as possible.

items.title: Escape from fire by walking low and fast
items.core: Dense smoke is more deadly than fire.
body: Cover your mouth and nose with a wet cloth and look for an exit along the wall.
Do not take the elevator or return to pick up items.

items.title: Aim the fire extinguisher at the root
items.core: Pull out the pin, aim, press, and shoot.
body: Evacuate immediately as the fire expands.

items.title: Protect your head first during an earthquake
items.core: Don't run in a hurry until the shaking stops.
body: Hide next to a solid bunker.

items.title: Clean small cuts first
items.core: 清洁比止血药更重要。

items.title: Cold compress first for sprain
items.core: Hot compress will aggravate swelling in the acute stage.

items.title: Do not rub foreign objects in the eyes
items.core: Rubbing may scratch the cornea.

items.title: Chemical Burns Flush Plenty
items.core: Dilution and flushing are key.

items.title: 预防窒息
items.core: 进食时避免说笑打闹。

items.title: 防坠落措施
items.core: 高处作业要固定。

items.title: Observe first after falling
items.core: Getting up immediately may aggravate the injury.
body: 感受疼痛部位和活动能力。

items.title: If the baby chokes on milk, he should lie on his side
items.core: to prevent the milk from being inhaled again.

items.title: Flush pet bites
items.core: There is a time limit for post-exposure treatment of rabies.

items.title: Observe allergies after bee stings
items.core: Most local reactions can be treated by yourself.
body: 出现全身症状立即就医。

items.title: Reduced activity after a snake bite
items.core: Slow down the spread of toxins.

items.title: Rewarm frostbite slowly
items.core: Rapid heating can cause damage.

items.title: Prevention is the key to drowning
items.core: Rescue is much more difficult than prevention.
body: Do not go to unsafe waters.
Full care for children during swimming.

items.title: Move to a cool place first for heat stroke
items.core: Cooling is the first priority.
body: Send medical attention immediately if you have abnormal consciousness.

items.title: Hypoglycemia requires quick sugar replenishment
items.core: Delay can damage the brain.
body: Ingest sugar as soon as you can swallow it.
Do not force feed when unconscious.

items.title: Severe allergies require immediate help
items.core: Laryngeal edema progresses quickly.
body: Use your medication as directed by your doctor.
Call the emergency number and explain your allergy history.

items.title: Fix suspected fractures first
items.core: Moving may cause secondary injuries.
body: Use splint or alternative to fix.
Apply ice and seek medical attention as soon as possible.

items.title: Observe for head impacts
items.core: Delayed symptoms can easily be ignored.
body: Pay attention to changes in consciousness, vomiting, and pupils.
Seek medical attention immediately if warning signs appear.

items.title: Be wary of heart problems if you have chest pain
items.core: Don’t endure persistent chest pain.
body: Stop activity and call emergency services.
Record the onset time and triggers.

items.title: Recognizing Signs of Stroke
items.core: Facial paralysis, arm weakness, difficulty speaking.
body: Record the time of symptom onset.

items.title: Protect your head during convulsions
items.core: Do not forcefully press the limbs.

items.title: Check breathing after syncope
items.core: Transient loss of consciousness requires evaluation.
body: Have the patient lie down and loosen the collar.
Seek medical attention if it happens repeatedly.

items.title: Sit up if you have difficulty breathing
items.core: A half-sitting position is more conducive to breathing.
body: Remain calm and call emergency services.
Use oxygen as directed by your doctor.

items.title: Do not relieve severe abdominal pain on your own
items.core: Covering up symptoms will delay diagnosis.
body: Record the location and nature of pain.
Seek medical attention as soon as possible.

items.title: See a doctor if a high fever persists
items.core: especially if it is accompanied by a change in consciousness.

items.title: Recognize dehydration
items.core: Dry mouth, oliguria, dizziness.

items.title: 药物过敏要停可疑药
items.core: 并保留药品信息。
body: Record the time of taking medication.
出现皮疹或呼吸困难立即就医。

items.title: 血糖异常要区分高低
items.core: 处理方向不同。

items.title: 哮喘发作按计划用药
items.core: 随身药不要放家里。
body: Ask for help immediately if it doesn’t work.

items.title: 心理危机要求助
items.core: 出现伤害自己的念头就是信号。

items.title: Observe the mental state of children with fever
items.core: Mental health is more important than body temperature.
body: Seek medical attention promptly if abnormality persists.

items.title: Have an emergency kit at home
items.core: Keep frequently used items within easy reach.
body: Put away flashlights, medicines, copies of IDs and water.

items.title: Plan two escape routes
items.core: There are alternatives if one is blocked.
body: Arrange a meeting point with your family.

items.title: Write important contacts on paper
items.core: The phone can still be used when the battery is out of power.
body: Take note of family, doctors and properties.
Place it in a fixed location.

items.title: Keep it refrigerated during a power outage
items.core: Opening the refrigerator will speed up the temperature rise.
body: Try not to open the door after a power outage.
Prepare lighting and charging equipment in advance.

items.title: Review afterwards
items.core: Review can turn experience into ability.
body: Record what is slow and what is missing.

items.title: The whole family participates in emergency drills
items.core: You will not panic if you know the process.
body: Let the children also know the meeting point.

items.title: Emergency contacts are posted in a fixed place
items.core: The mobile phone can be used even if the battery is low.
body: Teach your kids how to dial.

items.title: Have drinking water and ready-to-eat food available
items.core: Cover for at least three days.

items.title: Prepare backup lighting
items.core: When there is a power outage, give priority to using a flashlight.
body: The charging device is fully charged in advance.

items.title: Prepare radio equipment
items.core: Get information when the network is interrupted.

items.title: Compile a list of commonly used medications
items.core: Including dosage and allergy history.
body: Put it in the medicine box.

items.title: Consider pet emergencies
items.core: Pets need supplies and placement too.
body: Confirm the place where you can stay temporarily.

items.title: Prioritize the elderly and children
items.core: Do not leave them alone during evacuation.

items.title: 撤离清单提前写
items.core: 出门时按清单拿。
body: Place it in a fixed location.

items.title: Know community resources
items.core: Know nearby shelters and hospitals.

items.title: Insurance and document backup
items.core: Proof is required for post-disaster claims.

items.title: 准备备用电源
items.core: 保证通讯设备可用。

items.title: Fill the gaps with post-event review
items.core: Turn experience into improvement.
